event.summary: Removal of tests that launch legacy containers follows retirement
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc

## TLDR
The removed tests exercised container launches that this revision deliberately stops supporting; their removal is not itself a regression.

## Details
Assigned patch 00322-001 removes the real Podman terminal-host launch/Stop/Delete test and adds refusal tests for persisted retired sessions. The fixture at containerized_sessions.rs:43-105 creates an ordinary session, replaces its stored launch with legacy image_file configuration, restarts the supervisor, and asserts the stored old launch was loaded. The new refusal tests check the retired error, not merely any error. SPEC.md:4816-4823 at this revision says exactly: ‘The earlier experimental model, whose supervisor stayed outside the container and bind-mounted a host checkout, is retired. Existing sessions support Delete only. Opening terminals or tabs, exec, Stop, Restart, Clone, Replace and Replace with are refused. Delete retains the legacy container-removal path and confirms absence. Missing Podman counts as nothing left to remove.’ This explicitly accepts removing support for the old launch route. Suggested bucket: other for the considered coverage concern; confidence: confirmed by source and specification, no execution. proposed_drop: specification acceptance quoted above. Could-be-highest: no established shipped security or loss-of-work route from removing unsupported-launch coverage; deletion's retained cleanup contract still needs separate source inspection. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched.

## TLDR
Replacing tmux guards with terminal hosts does not by itself leave these real vendor agents running after a test panic.

## Details
Considered whether removing TmuxServerGuard caused orphaned real agents when assertions fail before explicit teardown. In real_agent_capture.rs:449 onward the work TestDir is declared before the supervisor state TestDir, so unwind drops state first. At this revision crates/farhelm-teststate/src/lib.rs:794-817 shows TestDir::drop calls end_hosts, which runs stop_hosts_within and keeps the state directory if cleanup cannot be confirmed. harness.rs:1139-1179 documents and stores the same guard in Harness before the semaphore permit. Explicit successful teardown uses end_all_terminals (harness.rs:2368-2382), asserting all owned hosts ended. The plain-command callback audit declares Harness after its probe/work directories, preserving the same order. Suggested bucket: other; confidence: confirmed source analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation; the state directory owns cleanup even during unwind. Could-be-highest: no; this concern is confined to opt-in maintainer tests and no catastrophic route is established. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Caveat: this establishes the cleanup mechanism and declaration order, not an observed successful cleanup on every OS or under every failure.

Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513

## TLDR
The removed test guarded against an agent accidentally running in another folder. Current launches refuse an inaccessible folder before executing the agent, so the removed tmux fallback scenario does not establish a current bug.

## Details
The deleted create_records_error_when_the_session_directory_cannot_be_entered fixture deliberately used the old-terminal constructor: tmux could fall back to HOME and the launch shim had to record Error. SPEC_impl.md:2015-2034 at this revision states ‘Every create starts its agent in a host, every new tab opens in one, and a Restart moves an agent out of tmux into one’. In crates/terminal-host/src/spawn.rs:577-581 the child calls chdir(prepared.cwd), calls fail(error_fd) on error, and only then execve; fail at :548-553 writes errno and exits. Thus current create cannot execute in a fallback folder through this path. SPEC.md:3761-3763 says ‘there is no launch without a working directory.’ The test's old retained-session/Error expectation is not the new host's pre-exec refusal contract. Suggested bucket: other for the considered test-removal concern; confidence: confirmed source analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation through unconditional host creation and fail-before-exec. Could-be-highest: the original hypothetical agent-in-wrong-folder consequence could damage user work, but no shipped route remains established by this removed case. This candidate is logged for the caller's independent drop check. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Caveat: no claim that every cwd identity or permission race is covered; this is restricted to the deleted test's fallback path.

Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513

The removed test guarded against an agent accidentally running in another folder. Current launches refuse an inaccessible folder before executing the agent, so the removed tmux fallback scenario does not establish a current bug.

The deleted create_records_error_when_the_session_directory_cannot_be_entered fixture deliberately used the old-terminal constructor: tmux could fall back to HOME and the launch shim had to record Error. In crates/terminal-host/src/spawn.rs:577-581 the child calls chdir(prepared.cwd), calls fail(error_fd) on error, and only then execve; fail at :548-553 writes errno and exits. Thus current create cannot execute in a fallback folder through this path. SPEC.md:3761-3763 says ‘there is no launch without a working directory.’ The test's old retained-session/Error expectation is not the new host's pre-exec refusal contract. event.summary: A permissive reset-view check cannot alone pass the identity audit
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 70bc66a9f285cc2a9984924f389834d118b7cfdc

## TLDR
The new screen-reset fallback is weaker than an exact closing notice, but it is followed by an independent check that the next prompt selects a different resumable conversation. It does not by itself let broken conversation capture pass.

## Details
Considered whether view_reset (real_agent_capture.rs:920-927, header present while the old answer and /new are absent) can misidentify a transient redraw as a completed /new. The helper reads the visible screen, not history: hosts/terminal.rs:2213-2223 and farhelm-terminal-emulator/src/emulator.rs:265-275 establish that contract. The actual test first requires the old answer via submit_prompt (:824-826), waits for the command popup, then after its reset wait asserts the old identity is retained and submits a distinct second prompt (:941-944). wait_for_reported_identity(:260-280), called with Some(&first), requires a different stored identity, a Resume offer, and the hook log's acknowledgement of the reported runtime. Thus a mistaken early reset observation alone is insufficient for success; failed command execution is caught by the independent identity assertion. StreamText is capped at 1 MiB and used for an exact old-identity notice, not row counts. Suggested bucket: other; confidence: confirmed source analysis of the assertions, no vendor execution. proposed_drop: source refutation of a false-pass route. Could-be-highest: no established security or lost-work route; the considered consequence is a weakened opt-in test oracle. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Caveat: this does not establish that every transient vendor redraw is handled without a test failure; that would require vendor execution, which was not requested.

## TLDR
Considered whether the new Codex invocation fails when PATH finds Codex through a relative directory, because the test launches from a different temporary folder. The old fixture already had the same limitation.

which_binary at reviewed :1316-1325 joins each PATH entry without canonicalizing it, and trusted_codex :1290-1302 places that result directly in the command launched under the private work directory. A relative entry could therefore resolve differently in the launched child. The parent fixture at :1247-1257 likewise resolves real_codex using the same helper and embeds that candidate directly in an exec command in its synthetic-home shim; the child starts in the same separate private work directory. Suggested bucket: other, opt-in fixture portability. Confidence: source-confirmed path handling and attribution; no execution, no claim about installed PATH. proposed_drop: no introduced change in the considered behavior. Could-be-highest: false; no security, user-work-loss or catastrophic maintainer-tooling route. possible_cover: none known; prohibited coverage sources not searched. Material caveat: this is not a claim that relative PATH entries work; only that the assigned rewrite did not create their failure mechanism.
